note: The pinned artefacts of the ESP32 machine path: the emulator, the chip's own mask ROM, and the MicroPython image it boots. Re-verify with the sha256 above; never patch in place.

artifacts.name: esp32sim (WebAssembly build, with the GPIO, I2C and SPI seams, and the ESP32-S2 machine)
artifacts.note: The emulator: it boots the chip's own mask ROM, the second-stage bootloader and an unmodified application. Unofficial and not affiliated with Espressif. This build carries five local patches in ../patches/: the GPIO seam, the I2C seam and the SPI seam (the bench seams), the corrected ESP32-S2/S3 system-timer register map, and the ESP32-S2 machine (the esp32s2 crate from the overlay under ../esp32s2/, wired into the wasm factory). scripts/build-esp32-wasm.mjs rebuilds it from upstream and the patches; the hash above is the toolchain's output, and the host family changes it. The S2 machine boots the S2 mask ROM and starts the app, but the application does not print the banner on the emulated path yet, so the S2 board is offered the interpreter only and the S2 leg is experimental. The classic ESP32 path is unchanged.

artifacts.name: MicroPython (ESP32 port, ESP32_GENERIC variant)
artifacts.note: The same MicroPython release the RP2 port is pinned to. A combined bootloader, partition table and application, flashed at 0x1000.

artifacts.name: ESP32 mask ROM (rev 3.0)
artifacts.note: Espressif's own mask ROM, the first thing the chip runs. The image the emulator boots from; rev 3.0 is the silicon the DevKit V1 carries.

artifacts.name: MicroPython (ESP32-S2 port, ESP32_GENERIC_S2 variant)
artifacts.note: The same MicroPython release the ESP32-S2 port ships. A combined bootloader, partition table and application, flashed at 0x1000. Pinned for the ESP32-S2 board. The S2 machine in esp32sim.wasm boots this image far into the app startup, but the banner never prints on the emulated path, so the board is offered the interpreter only.

artifacts.name: ESP32-S2 mask ROM (rev 0)
artifacts.note: Espressif's own mask ROM for the ESP32-S2, from the same esp-rom-elfs release as the classic ESP32 rev 3.0 ROM the emulator already boots. The first thing the S2 machine runs; it boots the combined image above far into the app startup, but the banner never prints on the emulated path.
